_about: THE PARITY LEDGER (upcoming/go-cli.md section 11, R2): where every Python CLI test went before it is deleted.
One entry per Python test class (per module-level function for test_bootstrap_secrets.py, which has no classes), keyed file::Name.
A value is {"go": ["<package>.<TestFunc>", "<package>.<TestFunc>/<subtest>", ...]} naming the Go tests that now carry the property,
or {"retired": "<kind>: <reason>"} with kind from the closed set held by both enforcement tests and a reason of at least 40 characters naming what replaces it.
An optional "note" states what inside a ported class was retired individually.
<package> is the directory under cli/internal/ (reconcile's external test package reconcile_test is keyed by its directory, reconcile).
<subtest> is the t.Run literal as Go's testing package reports it: spaces rewritten to underscores.
A Go test named in a retired reason (package.TestX) must exist too; both enforcements resolve those.
Enforcement A: tdd/unit/scripts/test_cli_parity_ledger.py (T1, ast.parse only, no imports) - keys == collected Python tests; every Go reference resolves.
Enforcement B: cli/internal/parity/ledger_test.go (TG, go/parser) - every Go reference still exists; a carrier cannot be deleted without editing this file.
survivors: classes in a ledger file that are NOT deleted at P4 (the corpus half of the contract test) and so have no disposition. Enforcement A checks they do not import the Python client.
Nothing here may be TBD. A missing carrier is an open problem in the plan, not a retirement.

tdd/unit/scripts/test_cli_debug.py::Test.note: The Python ScriptedSocket validated outbound frames with the server codec; the Go ScriptedSocket validates with debugproto.Decode, which the corpus pins to the server byte for byte.

python-websockets-specific: the two websockets-shape tests (rcvd-vs-flat close, legacy handshake exception) have no carrier; coder/websocket has one CloseError shape and one rejected-handshake response, there is nothing else to read.

click-specific: the two click-wiring tests (the placeholder attach is replaced on the group; the import happens lazily) have no carrier; cobra registers the real command directly and there is no placeholder to replace.

tdd/unit/scripts/test_cli_debug.py::Test.retired: python-websockets-specific: the dialer (coder/websocket) is compiled into the binary; no optional extra exists to be absent, and no version bound exists to be checked.

tdd/unit/scripts/test_cli_errors.py::Tes.note: The property is enforced by go/parser over the import lists (net/http only in internal/api, coder/websocket only in internal/terminal) instead of by grepping for httpx.

tdd/unit/scripts/test_cli_errors.py::Tes.retired: rich-specific: no markup language exists in the Go binary, so there is no renderer to feed bracketed text through; the property it guarded (untrusted text survives structurally) is ui.TestVerbatimQuoting.

tdd/unit/scripts/test_cli_tests_reconcil.note: Runs a REAL python -m pytest --collect-only over the fixture suite in cli/internal/reconcile/testdata; red on a box without pytest, by design.

tdd/unit/scripts/test_bootstrap_secrets..note: Six real processes re-executed through TestMain (LAZYAF_TEST_HELPER=init), so O_EXCL is exercised across processes as the Python test did.

tdd/unit/scripts/test_bootstrap_secrets..retired: python-interpreter: a static binary has no interpreter and no dependencies to be absent; the release smoke on a bare runner (release.yml, three OSes, no checkout) is the equivalent proof.

semantics-changed: the binary lives in ~/.local/bin, so 'beside itself' is meaningless; replaced by initcmd.TestRefusesUnmarkedDirectory - without a root marker init REFUSES and names --env-file instead of writing somewhere by guess.

tdd/unit/debug/test_terminal_protocol_co.retired: superseded-by-contract: the server emits constants.scalars/sets into tdd/contracts/debug_terminal.v1.json; debugproto.TestContractConstants and debugproto.TestContractReasons hold the Go codec to it, and TestCorpusIsCurrent (Python, kept) proves the file is fresh.

superseded-by-contract: every server->client frame is a corpus case with its exact wire string; debugproto.TestContractFrames decodes each and re-encodes it byte for byte, and debugproto.TestContractFramesCoverEveryType refuses a type the corpus forgot.

superseded-by-contract: every client->server frame is a corpus case whose wire string the server wrote; debugproto.TestContractFrames requires the Go encoder to reproduce it byte-identically, which is the old both-encoders-agree assertion with the server as the reference.

superseded-by-contract: the 16 malformed frames, the not-utf8 frame and the two encoder refusals are corpus cases; debugproto.TestContractMalformed refuses each with a ProtocolError and debugproto.TestContractRefusalsAreProtocolErrorsAndNothingElseIs keeps that the only error type.
superseded-by-contract: the encode/decode/reject vectors are the corpus base64 section, written by the server; debugproto.TestContractBase64 checks the Go codec against them with strict decoding.

superseded-by-contract: debugproto.TestEscapeKeysMapToWireCommands maps every escape key onto constants.scalars.COMMANDS from the corpus and debugproto.TestEscapeSurface pins the byte and the keys; TestEscapeSurfaceIsClientOnly (Python, kept) proves the server has no escape byte.

tdd/unit/packaging/test_wheel_build.py::.retired: packaging-wheel: there is no wheel; the artefact carries only the product because the binary is built with -trimpath and CGO_ENABLED=0 by scripts/build_cli.sh and proven by release.yml's smoke in a directory with no checkout.

packaging-wheel: there is no sdist; the source distribution is the git tag itself, resolvable by go install github.com/Brennan-VanderLaan/lazyaf/cli/cmd/lazyaf@<tag> because go.mod lives at the repo root.
packaging-wheel: a fresh machine can run it is now release.yml's three-OS smoke job, which installs the attached assets with cli/install.sh and runs the real binary with no checkout and no Python.

tdd/unit/packaging/test_wheel_metadata.p.retired: packaging-wheel: the version has no in-tree copy to keep single; the tag is stamped by -ldflags -X, checked across all six binaries by .github/scripts/check_binary_version.py (tdd/unit/scripts/test_check_binary_version.py) and version.TestDevBuildSaysDev keeps a plain build honest.

packaging-wheel: nothing is published to an index; the release page carries the binaries, checksums.txt and install.sh, and cli/README.md is the human-facing description the smoke's --help complements.
packaging-wheel: there is no console_scripts entry point; the binary IS the entry point, and the release smoke runs its --help and --version --short on every OS before publishing.
packaging-wheel: runtime dependencies are compiled in and hash-pinned by go.sum; go mod verify and go mod tidy with git diff --exit-code run in release.yml and pr-build.yml before any build.
packaging-wheel: there is no package list to keep explicit; the Go module's packages are the directories under cli/, walked by go vet ./... and go test ./... in the TG tier.

packaging-wheel: no .env or credential-shaped file can ship because nothing under cli/ is packaged as a tree; secret-scan.yml scans every tracked file, and cli/bin and cli/dist are gitignored build outputs.
